treatment.winner: THE FAUCET BEFORE THE WATER (comedian base)
grafts: dramatist: a tear-off calendar as the pressure clock, Dec 4 and Dec 7 the only circled pages, and the dog-door residents-only tag (MAY)
enthusiast: the residents-only option drawn as the one Alaska-first upside, valuable only if written down

explainer: tokenization drawn as a coat-check clerk (Marge) whose ticket is the record of who owns a stake, no coin or chart imagery, and the $20 million drawn as twenty fixed bags never scaled against anything or called idle
treatment.judge_reasoning: Two of three returned pitches independently reached a faucet or spigot before the water, because the angle is about order, not a verdict. A personified fixture with a want and nothing to pour is a neutral hero that implies no AI project the sources never name. The calendar gives the film a clock the viewer can check. The Test keeps the critic's card held unjoked. Showrunner synthesis, the scorer step was skipped because the pitches converged.

palette.sky: #8FA39A overcast pewter-sage lifting to pale straw #D8CFA3 at the horizon
palette.ground: #6B6A5E wet gravel lot with puddle glints
palette.hero: #C9A24B brushed brass, spent ONLY on Drip and his pipe fittings
palette.bucket: #7E868D darker galvanized pail, a squat dented trapezoid so the only round bright silhouette in frame is Drip
palette.rulebook: #D8432F tomato red, spent ONLY on the Rulebook and circled calendar dates
palette.paper: #D9D0B8 notice paper with #2A2620 warm graphite type, pulled below the brass highlight so the lightest value in a Drip shot is the brass specular
palette.accent: #5EEAD0 mint ONLY on the AI slip, the pitch
palette.mood: flat honest November overcast over a gravel lot, brass and mint where the question lives
palette.why: An Anchorage lot in November is gray gravel under cloud with spruce and mountains behind, so the world is honest. One gleaming brass object gives the eye a single place to follow.
palette.divergence: The last three films were raven dusk with lime (11-12), pink-gold ice fog with amber (11-11) and violet shore with vermilion (11-10). This is overcast pewter-sage gravel by day with brass, red and mint, no dusk, no lime, no pink-gold, no plum. Honest overlap: the Rulebook's tomato #D8432F is in the red family of 11-10 vermilion, 11-11 crimson and 11-12 stamp red. It is confined to one binder and the circled dates, and the film's one warm brass hero and mint slip carry the colour story. The ink moves to warm graphite #2A2620. Brass is also near 11-11's sodium amber in hue family, spent here on one hero only.
palette.value_check: L* approximately: gravel #6B6A5E 44, spruce #24402F 24, graphite #2A2620 17, pail #7E868D 55, sky #8FA39A 64, brass #C9A24B 68 with a specular #F2DE9A about 88 and a core shadow #6E5420 about 38, paper #D9D0B8 about 83. Drip and the pail are staged against the dark spruce row or the gravel from a raised eye line, never against open sky.
palette.ground_state: wet thawed gravel with puddle glints from the first frame, no frost. A first light flurry starts at the Rulebook's arrival (beat 37, 101.42s) and dusts the lot by the button, the only snow in the film.

light.time_of_day: flat overcast day on the lot with the straw horizon band behind, paper-lit cutaways, one glowing mint slip, a hard cut to black
light.arc: the cloud ceiling lowers and the straw band narrows each act, so the lot goes from open overcast (act 1) to grey flat (act 2) to a darker grey (act 3) and a first flurry in act 4, a clock you can see
light.direction: soft top light from the cloud with soft contact shadows only, brass lit from the straw horizon band as a warm rim from camera-left so it stays gold

per_shot.2: warm interior paper light from the high hall windows, a cool window onto the lot
per_shot.3: overcast, pump house and booth flat-lit, flag the only motion
per_shot.4: macro, brass rim on the clamp and Drip's neck
per_shot.5: cutaway lit by the counter lamp, warm work-lamp light, no mint
per_shot.6: low overcast, the stencil paint matte, padlock steel highlight
per_shot.7: billboard flat-lit, the mint slip the only emissive object
per_shot.8: overhead flat paper light on the ledger, soft ring shadows, Drip as a small corner inset lit by the lot's overcast
per_shot.9: greying overcast, the straw band narrowing behind the lifting pipe

light.depth_approach: lib/stage3d planes, spruce row and Chugach ridges in parallax behind the lot, a long pipe receding in perspective, stacked interior planes for the hall, coat check and boardroom

shape_language: PRIMARY axis: Drip's round eyes and curved neck against the long straight horizontal of the pipe to the horizon. SECONDARY: rectilinear paper, calendar pages and signs. WHY: a curved hopeful face at the end of a hard straight line is the image of a faucet before the water.

casting.hero: DRIP, a brass yard spigot with a face (local component in the episode file, handle brow, neck eyes), the declared hero and throughline, five states staged where he is on screen
casting.throughline: Drip: bare and dry over an empty pail, plumbed in with a second cough, padlocked and tagged with brass dulled, handle quarter turned toward the Rulebook beside him, still dulled and dry with the key at his feet
supporting: BUCKET, a squat dented trapezoid pail with a tired kind face, the would-be Alaskan investor waiting under the dry spout from shot 1 to shot 12, never a person or a named group
THE RULEBOOK, a tomato-red three-ring binder with one eye, a tiny speck walking toward Drip from the spruce row in shot 1 and arriving out of breath at 101s
MARGE, an ordinary coat check clerk in a parka (local figure in the episode file, no likeness of anyone real), her ledger blank until the ticket

local props in the episode file, none from the shelf: pump house with AIDEA flag, booth with funnel, twenty bags, gauge, cable car clamp, billboard and speech balloon, magnifying glass and mint slip, ledger, masthead, two cup nameplates, seven coffee rings, Lower 48 outline and crate, boardroom table and chairs, wall calendar, roadside signs, plank tag, padlock and key, dust speck, press podium with state seal and a notice-paper banner, ghost server hall in the window, OPEN flip sign, torn price tag, paperwork pile, name tab, governor nameplate and post, second sign over the gate, coat, hook and half door
casting.net_new: none from the shelf, every named prop is local to Ep1113.tsx. dedupe.py check --hero Drip returned FRESH

motion_language: Drip leans toward whoever walks up, coughs dust, and his handle lifts like a brow. Signs swing on springs. Calendar pages tear with anticipation and fall. Bags thump with squash. The whole frame jolts only on the three board kicks.

composition.focal_hierarchy: each shot names one 55 to 70 percent hero, a 20 to 30 percent support and 10 to 15 percent world
composition.info_placement: plates live on objects (signs, tags, calendar pages, the critic card), lower third on a minority of beats
composition.negative_space: the long empty lot and the black after the hard cut
composition.safe_area: hero and plates within y 420 to 1500 of the 9:16 master
composition.signature_shot: shot 12 as one move: macro on the padlock key at Drip's feet, then a low pull back along the pipe until Drip is small at its end against the spruce row, the pail empty under his lip, the speck hanging and a hard cut to black, rhyming with the shot 1 pipe reveal
